stories.title: 'I would love to see him be back': Trump urges Nvidia to give Jensen Huang 'second chance'
summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday called for AI giant Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang after he was ousted as CEO over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. “I would love to see him be back.
Earlier, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that Trump did not discuss Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting this week.
Responding to a question, Bessent told US broadcaster CNBC that Huang had not come up in Trump’s talks with Xi, held earlier this week in Shenzhen.

stories.title: Indian man jailed over US murder plot against Sikh separatist
summary: US federal prosecutors alleged that an Indian intelligence officer, who remains at large, directed the plot and recruited Gupta in May 2023 to hire a hitman to carry out the murder.
Canada separately alleged in 2023 that India arranged a plot on its soil that ended in the killing of a Sikh separatist, who was a naturalised Canadian citizen.

Hardeep Singh Nijjar, 45, was shot dead by masked gunmen outside the Sikh temple he presided over after being wanted by Indian authorities for alleged terrorism offences and conspiracy to commit murder — accusations he denied.

stories.title: Minister insists referendum on new provinces 'will happen'
summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Friday insisted that a referendum on the formation of new provinces “will happen”.
Bilawal had expressed his opposition to the creation of provinces and the idea of holding a referendum for such a move in his speech.
Soon after Bilawal’s remarks, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar defended the move, saying it was a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion.

stories.title: CTD says 3 terrorists, including mastermind of Kohat police lines attack, killed in IBO
summary: PESHAWAR: The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) on Friday claimed to have killed three terrorists of the banned Ittehadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), including the mastermind of the Kohat Police Lines attack in September.
According to an official statement, the Kohat CTD received intelligence that armed terrorists of the banned IMP had set up a checkpoint on Bazeed Khel Road in Kohat.
The statement read that according to preliminary information, two of the suspected terrorists killed had been identified as Abdul Hai and Abdul Rashid.

stories.title: ECC allows 416,000T sugar export
summary: The government on Friday allowed the export of another 416,000 metric tonnes of sugar without circulating the summary among the relevant ministries, amid its failure to deregulate the sugar sector despite a condition by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The ECC's approval for the export of 416,000 tonnes of sugar was the third such permission in four months, bringing the total export quantity to 724,000 metric tonnes for this season.
According to a draft of the National Policy for De-regulation of the Sugar Sector, over the last decade, Pakistan exported 3.92 million tonnes of sugar but also imported about 565,000 metric tonnes.

stories.title: SPI stays elevated in double digits
summary: The year-on-year increase continues to be led by sharp rises in energy-related items, including liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) up 87.99%, electricity charges for the lowest consumption quintile up 36.30%, high-speed diesel up 24.84%, and petrol up 21.35%.

The sustained double-digit year-on-year SPI reading comes against the backdrop of prolonged regional tensions that have disrupted energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz and kept international oil and LPG prices elevated for much of the year.
The monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased by 9.6% year-on-year in October 2026 as compared to a rise of 10.3% in the previous month and 6.2% in October 2025.

stories.title: SOEs scrap LPG auctions after LHC intervention
summary: The LPG auctions planned by state-owned enterprises (SOEs) Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL), Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL) and Pak-Arab Refinery Limited (PARCO) have been scrapped, the Pakistan LPG Marketers Association (PLPGMA) announced.

The association argued that the proposed process was contrary to the legal and regulatory framework governing the LPG sector that prohibits LPG producers from charging any sort of premium over and above the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) notified price.

Separately, the LPG Distributors Association of Pakistan issued a pre-litigation representation challenging the Federal Cabinet's LPG Pricing Guidelines approved on November 4, 2026, and communicated by the Petroleum Division on November 5, 2026.

stories.title: Resilience cannot be substitute for economic growth
summary: Adil Salahuddin called for stronger private sector financing and deeper capital markets to support business expansion and economic transformation.

The discussion underscored the need for coordinated improvements in financing, digital infrastructure, regulatory practices, governance and workforce development to strengthen the competitiveness of Pakistani businesses.
His address focused on the importance of entrepreneurial activity in generating solutions to changing economic conditions and supporting business transformation.

stories.title: Trump not sure if denuclearisation 'can ever happen'
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Friday he was not sure that denuclearisation 'can ever happen', describing his trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as highly positive.
On Ukraine, Trump described his talks with Putin as "very good".

He said he was working towards a deal that would be fair to the United States, adding: "Time for Canada to stop ripping us off." On Mexico, however, Trump indicated that negotiations were closer to completion, saying the two countries were "getting close to a deal".

stories.title: Russian missiles land in Poland amid NATO drills
summary: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday during a major Russian bombardment of neighbouring Ukraine, prompting Warsaw to describe the incidents as a likely provocation and NATO to call them a violation of Polish airspace.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incidents appeared to be an intentional provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in southeastern Poland, where troops are preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.
There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the missiles, the suspected drone or the military exercises.

stories.title: Saudi forces launch major strikes in Yemen
summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis launched a series of strikes on the Red Sea port of Hodeida and other targets on Friday, as the rebels threatened retaliatory attacks on Saudi ports, power facilities and aviation, raising fears of a wider escalation.
In a separate development, the Saudi-led coalition said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards Jazan province.

Saudi-backed government forces recently withdrew from areas near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, while the Houthis advanced towards Aden, the government's interim capital after the group seized Sanaa in 2014.

stories.title: PM ties offshore exploration to energy security
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday linked exploration of potential oil and gas reserves in Pakistan's maritime boundaries to the country's energy security and economic development.
He also welcomed Turkey's Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, Alparslan Bayraktar, and thanked the Turkish government and people for standing alongside Pakistan.
The Oruç Reis will bring together Turkish scientific expertise and the experience of Pakistan's national energy companies to conduct advanced exploration in the country's offshore domain, he said.

stories.title: FO rebuffs Delhi over mineral wealth
summary: Pakistan on Friday strongly rejected India's remarks at a recent United Nations Security Council Arria-formula meeting on natural resources, describing them as an attempt to interfere in its internal affairs.

The spokesperson also welcomed the meeting of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia in Shenzhen, describing it as a positive development that could help ease tensions among major powers and promote global peace.
Asked how Pakistan could benefit from the emerging engagement among the three powers, Sajjad said Islamabad had traditionally maintained good relations with all major global players.

stories.title: Minister schools Indian media over 'terror mantra'
summary: DELHI Federal Minister for Climate Change Dr Musadik Malik has said rather than focusing on a single incident of terror or Pakistan-India bilateral issues, it will be far better to address the problems of the entire region through a structured mechanism and concrete evidence.

Earlier, Dr Musadik Malik also stressed the importance of civilisational dialogue among regional countries, including Pakistan and India, saying that cultures and historical connections transcend geographical and political boundaries.

He emphasised that civilisational dialogue among regional countries was an important contemporary need, particularly between Pakistan and India, where shared historical and cultural connections provided scope for greater mutual understanding.

stories.title: 'Retaliation' won't weaken us: Fazl
summary: Addressing party workers at a gathering after Friday prayers in Peshawar, Fazl said his party had refused to recognise "a fabricated electoral mandate" or join the government despite repeated requests over the past two and a half years.

He alleged that the government had subsequently resorted to threats of reopening cases against party leaders, but warned that such pressure would not weaken JUI-F or force it to abandon its political position.
However, after JUI-F refused to accept "a fabricated mandate" and declined to join the government, Fazl said, the party was threatened with the reopening of cases against its leaders.

stories.title: PTI backs referendum on new provinces
summary: Amir Dogar, PTI's chief whip in the National Assembly, has endorsed the idea of holding a referendum on the question of creating new provinces in the country while urging that new administrative units should be created according to the law and the Constitution.
He said the PTI would hold comprehensive political consultations on new provinces and also discuss the issue at the PTI core and political committee meetings.

Talking to the media in Peshawar, PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan said the PTI would take a stance on the question of new provinces after reviewing the draft of the alleged 28th amendment and holding consultations with other parties.

stories.title: Pakistan logs 9.4 million annual cyberattacks
summary: Pakistan recorded more than 9.4 million cyberattacks over the past 12 months, with over 6.3 million devices targeted by cyber threats, according to a report by cybersecurity firm Kaspersky.
It said 24% of Kaspersky users in Pakistan encountered cyber threats targeting their devices, while 15% faced risks involving phishing and web-based attacks.
More than 448,000 exploit attacks were recorded in Pakistan over the past year, although the number declined by 8% compared with the previous year.

stories.title: Corruption vulnerabilities identified in govt institutions in bid to undertake ‘self-accountability’, says law minister
summary: The federal government has identified weaknesses that could create opportunities for corruption in ten institutions through a comprehensive ‘National Risk Assessment of Corruption Vulnerabilities’ survey, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said on Friday.

Shifting his attention back to the report, the law minister stated that the report had highlighted “checks and balances, misuse of authority” to stop financial leakages. “This has been done for the guidance of the federal institutions.
The law minister said the objective of the report was to move towards “self-accountability” and ensure federal institutions operate on the basis of merit and transparency without any lapses.

stories.title: The provinces diatribe
summary: The consolation is that they have agreed to pursue a path of political reconciliation and kickstart a debate on the utility of creating more provinces.
The issue of creating more provinces is a national concern and should not be pursued through quick-fix mechanisms.

The rejoinder from the Presidency, however, stating that the leaders also "discussed the previous constitutional amendments", noting that all coalition parties had introduced these through mutual consultation, is a setback to Bilawal's stance.

stories.title: Trillion-rupee cyber fraud
summary: The network allegedly funneled gambling proceeds through commercial banks, microfinance institutions, mobile wallets, shell companies and 'mule accounts', including one settlement account that alone received Rs3.72 billion in less than two years.
A study by Visa found roughly one in two Pakistanis experienced online financial fraud in 2024, and annual losses from digital fraud may reach $9 billion about 2.5% of GDP.
Without heavy penalties and better enforcement, there is no incentive to discourage people from indulging in scams, especially when scammers know how easily an arrested person can be made to go home.

stories.title: Fresh hope
summary: Pakistan's eight-wicket win over Sri Lanka in the second Test at Rawalpindi sealed a 1-0 series result, following a draw in the opening game.
It is also Pakistan's first Test series win in two years - and their first in the current World Test Championship cycle.
First, prepare sporting, pace-friendly pitches at home that test batters and consistently reward seamers.

stories.title: An elegy of unbelonging
summary: Had this book pretended to be anything more than an honest emotional chronicle of a life in the public eye, we would have seen present-day Mrs Gandhi sitting behind a wooden desk, signing important-looking documents under a title like 'My Struggle' or 'My Destiny'.
Rajiv Gandhi comes out looking rather well here.
When the backlash arrives, she shares the unvarnished dread for her brother-in-law's life, followed by a frugal existence in exile from power.

stories.title: Justice lies in conscience, not buildings
summary: Earlier, the Geneva-based Stop Killer Robots, a human rights organisation, had fired Noor for speaking out at the UN against Israeli occupation and genocide of Palestinians in Gaza that had begun after the Hamas October 7 attacks.

Ironical as much as hypocritical that an organisation publicly avows opposition to Israel using Palestinians as "guinea pigs to test these weapons ( killer robots)" but punishes its own employee for calling out Israeli atrocities.

Noor's case also exposed as to who gets to speak about Palestine, and whether a lawyer can challenge the thus far predominant consensus on Israeli apartheid and genocide without risking their livelihood.

stories.title: Cheapest village development project
summary: I believe we should introduce a village property-sharing scheme that turns abandoned and unused houses into useful community spaces.

With the owner's permission, these buildings could become small libraries, tuition centres, food-storage facilities, women's skill-development workshops, first-aid centres, digital learning rooms and emergency shelters.
Give a house another purpose, and a village gains a future.

stories.title: A good cop’s guide to reporting rape
summary: Duties from the CrPC (s.154, Schedule II) and the Anti-Rape Crisis Cell manual by Dr Summaiya Syed, Police Surgeon Karachi (ch.
Police data from Sindh provides a troubling picture of reported rape cases: In 2025, 178 cases were reported across Sindh.
The data tells us that Sindh has recorded almost three-quarters of the number of rape cases registered during the entire previous year.

stories.title: Pakistan’s natural resources worth $8-10tr at 'most conservative estimate', says Dar
summary: He noted that Oruc Reis brought “Turkish scientific expertise together with the experience and capabilities of our national energy companies to advance exploration in Pakistan’s offshore domain”.

He thanked Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan for sending Oruc Reis to Pakistan and for Türkiye’s cooperation in the offshore oil and gas exploration project, welcoming the growing cooperation between Pakistan and Türkiye in the energy sector.

The exploration of potential oil and gas reserves in Pakistan’s maritime areas was an “important step” towards strengthening the country’s energy security and promoting economic development, the prime minister said.

stories.title: Afghanistan not invited to ECO moot as Islamabad does not recognise Kabul regime: FO
summary: The Foreign Office (FO) said on Friday that Afghanistan was not invited to participate in the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Islamabad as Pakistan does not recognise the incumbent Afghan regime.
Addressing a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said that Afghanistan’s membership had been suspended by the ECO Secretariat.

Islamabad MoU ‘impeded’ The spokesperson also addressed the implementation of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the US and Iran in June, saying that it “unfortunately remains impeded”.

stories.title: Pakistan Shaheens begin Asia Cup Rising Stars title defence with 61-run win over UAE
summary: In reply, UAE were dismissed for 184 in 40.5 overs as Pakistan Shaheens’ bowlers maintained control of the chase.
Fast bowler Ali Raza struck early, removing three top-order batters to leave UAE struggling at 16 for three inside the first six overs.
Mohammad Shahdad top-scored for UAE with 45 off 60 balls, including four fours and a six, while Aftab Alam made 39 and Awais Ali Shah added 32.

stories.title: 'We don't want to die': Protesters slam Claude creator Anthropic after IPO debut
summary: Anthropic, which on Thursday pulled off the largest IPO in history, says it has not yet reached the RSI stage.
Anthropic was founded by several former OpenAI employees who disagreed with its business decisions and vowed to always prioritise safety. “Stop the AI race,” another protest sign said.
With Anthropic, maybe I’ll live 10 years longer,” Gila said. “Or maybe you’ll die in like two years,” the other demonstrator responded.

stories.title: Khawaja Asif urges Zardari to intervene in debate over new provinces
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Friday urged President Asif Ali Zardari to intervene in the ongoing debate over the creation of new provinces, calling for a unified national approach to resolve the issue.

Speaking on a private television programme, Naya Pakistan, the minister said the government wanted to obtain the people's opinion through a democratic process and was trying to build consensus among political parties. “The referendum will take place.

Referring to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's recent remarks, he said the PPP leader had the right to express his party's position on the creation of a province in Sindh but should not have gone beyond the issue to criticise other political parties.

stories.title: FO rejects India's 'undiplomatic, irresponsible' remarks about Pakistan's mineral wealth
summary: The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday categorically rejected the “undiplomatic and irresponsible” remarks made by India at the United Nations regarding the country’s mineral wealth.

The remarks had come after Pakistan raised the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) during the meeting, which has been held in abeyance by India following the attack in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26.
In response to Harish’s remarks, Pakistan’s First Secretary Ansar Shah rejected the “frivolous and highly inappropriate remarks”.

stories.title: Gohar demands end to ‘harassment’ of PTI workers, says 29 lawmakers arrested, missing
summary: PTI has claimed that arrests of party workers intensified after the party announced its long march.
On September 22, National Assembly member Fazal Khan from Charsadda was said to have been taken from Rashakai.
Provincial Assembly member Muhammad Riaz from Kolai-Palas was reported missing on Sept 25, while Sultan Rom, the MPA from Swat, was taken by unidentified persons the next day.

stories.title: Short-term inflation reaches 10.41pc on costly flour
summary: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation was recorded at 10.41 per cent year-on-year in the week ending on Nov 19, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.
Meanwhile, the prices of 20 items remained unchanged from the previous week.
Items that recorded week-on-week price declines included tomatoes (30.55pc), onions (9.17pc), LPG (6.46pc), petrol (3.87pc), diesel (2.46pc), pulse moong (0.54pc), gur (0.08pc) and sugar (0.07pc).

stories.title: COP31 venue failed the disability access challenge
summary: Mustafa Ertok, COP31’s accessibility lead, was quoted saying that “we have met the needs of all 521 participants, both in transportation and within the venue,” and that accessibility was being treated “not as a preference, but as a human right”.
Quiet and decompression spaces were “being explored,” with information to be provided “if these spaces are confirmed” (cop31.tr/accessibility).
The International Disability Alliance, at its Disability Climate Caucus press conference at COP31, made the same point in structural terms: “Accessibility cannot be limited to physical access alone.

stories.title: Bilawal wants PM Shehbaz to become first premier to complete 5-year term
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Friday that he wanted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to become the first premier to complete a five-year term in office.
I will not do that […] I am saying that I want Shehbaz Sharif to be the first prime minister […] to complete a five-year term,” Bilawal said.
Bilawal noted that the prime minister had not been “given the chance” to focus on the economic issues so far. “What can he do?

stories.title: Settling disputes
summary: WITH almost 2m court cases clogging the lower judiciary — most of them in Punjab — Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s nod to a proposed panchayat system to resolve local-level disputes is expected to be well received by many litigants.

For instance, India’s village justice court system aimed at providing inexpensive and accessible justice to rural communities in the country, has had mixed results that should provide a useful clue for the government here.

Small steps towards the larger goal of an integrated justice system will allow the authorities to ensure accessible legal relief for Pakistan’s rural communities — measures that are sensitive to local concerns without straying from constitutional norms.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs1, increases diesel by Rs2 till Nov 23
summary: The federal government on Friday decreased the price of petrol by Rs1 while increasing high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2 per litre till November 23.

Read: Petrol hiked by Re1 On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.

stories.title: On North Waziristan visit, CDF Munir vows to eliminate terrorism, preserve peace in KP
summary: Security forces continue to carry out counterterrorism action in KP and Balochistan, the two provinces that have been particularly affected by terrorism in Pakistan.

Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37 per cent, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57pc, and injuries decreasing by 71pc compared to September, the report said.

The merged districts of KP recorded 30 attacks during October, compared with 34 in September, and deaths resulting from these attacks decreased from 33 to 25, while injuries increased from 11 to 13, the report said.

stories.title: Musadik Malik arrives in New Delhi to attend SCO dialogue forum
summary: Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Dr Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.
Recent high-level engagements between Pakistan and India have largely taken place under the SCO framework; for instance, Bilawal’s visit in 2023 and Jaishankar’s in 2024.
Pakistan has assumed the rotating chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for the 2026-27 term and is scheduled to host the organisation’s summit in Islamabad in August 2027.
